title: Accessibility Engineering Playbook

claim_stubs.name: Fitts's Law (Shannon Formulation)
claim_stubs.engineering_meaning: Movement time to a target increases with Index of Difficulty ID = log2(A/W + 1), where A is amplitude (distance) and W is target width; MT = a + b·ID.
claim_stubs.how_to_detect_violations: Estimate A from resting cursor/thumb zones and W of primary CTAs; flag frequent actions with high ID or targets below WCAG floor.
claim_stubs.when_to_apply: CTA placement, toolbars, menus, drag targets on pointer UIs.
claim_stubs.when_not_to_apply: Pure keyboard flows; voice; intentionally high-friction destructive controls.

claim_stubs.name: Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)
claim_stubs.engineering_meaning: When a component receives keyboard focus, it must not be entirely hidden by author-created content.
claim_stubs.how_to_detect_violations: Tab through the page with sticky chrome present; fail if focused element is completely covered.
claim_stubs.when_to_apply: All interactive components, especially with sticky UI chrome.
claim_stubs.when_not_to_apply: User-opened content (e.g., modal) dismissible without advancing focus, per WCAG nuance.

claim_stubs.name: Minimum Touch Target Size
claim_stubs.engineering_meaning: Interactive elements on touchscreens must have a minimum physical rendered size of 1cm x 1cm (0.4in x 0.4in) or adhere to standard design system sizing tokens (e.g., 44px/48px) to ensure accurate selection and prevent accidental taps.
claim_stubs.how_to_detect_violations: Measure the physical rendered dimensions or inspect CSS for standard sizing tokens on interactive elements. Verify that both height and width meet the minimum threshold (e.g., 1cm or 44px/48px) and are not hardcoded to smaller, non-compliant pixel values.
claim_stubs.when_to_apply: Apply to all interactive elements (buttons, links, icons) on touchscreen interfaces, or when adopting a token-based design system for consistent hit areas.
claim_stubs.when_not_to_apply: Do not apply to non-interactive, purely decorative elements, or strictly to mouse-driven desktop interfaces. Do not limit to the minimum size when the context involves movement or specific audiences (e.g., children, seniors) requiring even larger targets.

claim_stubs.name: WCAG 2.2 Target Size (Minimum)
claim_stubs.engineering_meaning: Pointer targets must be at least 24×24 CSS pixels, or satisfy the spacing exception with a 24 CSS-pixel diameter circle that does not intersect other targets.
claim_stubs.how_to_detect_violations: Measure CSS bounding boxes. If width or height < 24px, test whether a 24px-diameter circle centered on the box intersects any other target.
claim_stubs.when_to_apply: All pointer-activated controls (mouse, touch, pen), including icon-only buttons.
claim_stubs.when_not_to_apply: Inline text links constrained by line-height; unmodified user-agent controls; equivalent larger control available; essential/legal presentation exceptions per WCAG.

claim_stubs.name: WCAG Contrast (Minimum)
claim_stubs.engineering_meaning: Text and images of text must maintain at least 4.5:1 contrast against the background; large text at least 3:1.
claim_stubs.how_to_detect_violations: Automated contrast checkers (axe, WAVE, WebAIM) plus sampling computed styles on text over images/gradients.
claim_stubs.when_to_apply: All meaningful text and images of text, including form labels and error copy.
claim_stubs.when_not_to_apply: Decorative text, inactive/disabled components, incidental logotypes as allowed by WCAG.

claim_stubs.name: Steering Law (Accot-Zhai)
claim_stubs.engineering_meaning: The time required to navigate a constrained 2D path is proportional to the length of the path divided by its width. For a straight tunnel, T = a + b(A/W), where A is length and W is width.
claim_stubs.how_to_detect_violations: Identify UI elements requiring continuous path navigation (e.g., nested hover menus). Measure the path length (A) and width (W). High A/W ratios indicate usability bottlenecks.
claim_stubs.when_to_apply: Designing hierarchical cascading menus, sliders, scrollbars, drag-and-drop interactions, and drawing tools.
claim_stubs.when_not_to_apply: Simple point-and-click tasks without path constraints (use Fitts's Law instead), or keyboard-only navigation.

claim_stubs.name: Keystroke-Level Model (KLM) Time Prediction
claim_stubs.engineering_meaning: Task execution time can be estimated by summing the times of physical-motor operators (Keystroking, Pointing, Homing, Drawing), mental preparation (M), and system response (R).
claim_stubs.how_to_detect_violations: Map out a frequent user task and sum the KLM operators. If the predicted time exceeds business requirements, the workflow is too complex and requires simplification.
claim_stubs.when_to_apply: Optimizing high-frequency, repetitive tasks in keyboard and mouse interfaces.
claim_stubs.when_not_to_apply: Touch interfaces (use TLM instead), highly exploratory tasks, or tasks dominated by complex problem-solving rather than interaction.
